title: WHAT THE DATA SAY: 63% say their work personality differs greatly from who they are day to day
body_markdown:
By: Ray Day


## **CONTACT:**


Ray Day
ray.day@stagwellglobal.com


*We wanted to share our latest consumer and business insights, based on research from[Stagwell](https://www.stagwellglobal.com/) and[Allison Worldwide](https://www.allisonworldwide.com/) .* *Among the highlights of our weekly* *consumer sentiment tracking:*


**SPLIT OFFICE PERSONALITIES**


Job seekers recognize that adapting to a new workplace’s culture is important, yet 2 in 3 say their personality at work is different from who they really are, according to our Harris Poll research with[Express Employment Professionals](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/98-of-job-seekers-say-adapting-to-workplace-culture-is-important-but-more-than-half-call-it-unfair-302872799.html) .


- 98% of job seekers say adapting to workplace culture is important.
- Yet 63% say their work persona differs greatly from who they are day to day.
- 80% of Gen Z have changed their personality to fit workplace culture – 69% for Millennials, 59% for Gen X and 50% for Boomers.
- 83% believe employees who do not conform to office culture do not stay with a company long.
- Many job seekers question whether personality should carry that much weight: 56% say personality has nothing to do with their work or ability to do the job, including 71% of Gen Z, 54% of millennials, 51% of Gen X and 36% of Boomers.
- *See also:*[The average job seeker now needs to apply to 400 to 750 jobs to land a single offer](https://thenextbigthink.substack.com/p/doomjobbing-deepfakes-and-a-broken)


**WHAT’S FOR DINNER?**


Americans are stressed less by cooking than by figuring out what to cook, according to Harris Poll research with[Instacart](https://investors.instacart.com/news-releases/news-release-details/meet-clementine-instacarts-ai-shopping-assistant-takes-whats) .


- 80% of Americans say figuring out what to make for dinner causes them stress.
- A third say the hardest part isn’t the cooking; it’s deciding what to make.
- 3 in 5 say would use AI assistant to help determine what’s best for dinner tonight.


**SIGNS STILL SELL**


Business signage deeply influences where Americans shop, what they trust and which brands they remember, according to The Harris Poll and[Signarama](https://signarama.com/signage-survey-2026) .


- 84% say business signage affects their decision to make a purchase, and 39% have entered a business solely because of its sign.
- 93% say signage affects whether they remember a business, while 91% say it helps a business stand out from competitors.
- 9 in 10 say signage affects whether a business appears professional or high quality, and 75% say chaotic or hard-to-read signage makes a business seem less credible.
- 41% have struggled to locate a business because its sign was difficult to read.
- 17% have decided not to enter a business because of its signage.
